explanations.explanation: You've got it, baker. The text says "As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue…" (Acts 17:2). A custom is just a habit, and Paul has a good one. Mine? I check the oven every four minutes like the cookies might have packed up and moved out. They're STILL in there. They're ALWAYS in there. They have NOWHERE else to be!

Not quite, baker. The text says "As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue…" (Acts 17:2). So the answer is True. A custom is a habit, like me peeking at the oven timer when I know it hasn't rung.
That's it, baker. Acts 17:2 says Paul "…reasoned with them from the Scriptures…" That's the Word of God on the table. And it goes on for three Sabbaths.

Close, but that's not what the text says. Acts 17:2 says Paul "…reasoned with them from the Scriptures…" Nothing in this passage mentions visions. His whole case is built on the Word of God, and I like that kind of recipe.

I see why you'd go there, baker, but this passage never mentions Greek poets. It says Paul "…reasoned with them from the Scriptures…" (Acts 17:2). He's standing in a Jewish synagogue, so the Scriptures are the book on the table.
Right on the money, baker. Paul explains and proves "…that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead." (Acts 17:3). Both parts go together, and he shows them from the Scriptures.

Good guess, baker, but the text says something different. Paul is explaining that the Christ "…had to suffer and rise from the dead." (Acts 17:3). The word is suffer. Paul's proving something about what had to happen to Christ.

Waiting feels natural, baker, I do a lot of it by the oven. But Acts 17:3 says the Christ "…had to suffer and rise from the dead." The word there is suffer. Paul is showing them what the Scriptures say about what Christ had to go through.

Not this time, baker. Acts 17:4 says "Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas…" Silas is Paul's traveling partner, and some of the Jews joined them. So the statement is False, because some were persuaded.
Yes, baker, False. "Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas…" (Acts 17:4). Silas is Paul's traveling partner. Those three Sabbaths of reasoning didn't go unheard.
You nailed it, baker. The text says "…a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women." joined them (Acts 17:4). It's a big crowd, and it isn't only the Jews in it.
I get the guess, since Rome is in the background of this whole passage. But Acts 17:4 says "…a large number of God-fearing Greeks…" The word is Greeks, and Romans don't show up in that verse.
Different country, baker, but a good try. Acts 17:4 says "…a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women." Egyptians aren't mentioned anywhere in this passage.

That's right, baker. Acts 17:5 says they "…brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar." Notice the jealousy comes first. Then the troublemakers show up.

explanations.answer: Report them to the high priest
explanations.explanation: Not quite, baker. The text says nothing about a high priest here. Acts 17:5 says they brought in troublemakers from the marketplace and formed a mob. A report is quiet, and this was loud.

A debate would've been tidy, baker, but that's not what the text says happens. Acts 17:5 says they "…brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar." What we get is a mob and an uproar.

Not this time, baker. Acts 17:5 says they raided Jason's house in search of Paul and Silas, and verse 6 says "…when they could not find them…" So the mob doesn't find them there. The statement is False.

That's it, baker. Acts 17:6 says "…when they could not find them…" so the mob raids Jason's house and comes up empty. Jason is a man in Thessalonica, and since they couldn't find Paul and Silas, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials instead.

Yes, baker. They shout that all these men are "…defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!" (Acts 17:7). Caesar is the Roman emperor, so that's the charge they pick. The mob says it right after saying Jason welcomed them into his home.
Not quite, baker. Nothing in this passage mentions stealing or a temple. The mob says they're "…defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!" (Acts 17:7).

Taxes would be a bold charge, baker, but it isn't what the text says. In Acts 17:7 the mob says they're "…defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!" The charge is about a king, not money.

explanations.answer: Bond is collected and they are released
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. Acts 17:9 says "…they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them." Jason is the one the mob said had welcomed Paul and Silas into his home. He and the others walk out once the bond is collected.

That did happen to Paul and Silas in Philippi (Acts 16:22-23), but it's not what happens here. In Thessalonica, "…they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them." (Acts 17:9). Different city, different ending.

I see where that comes from, baker. Paul and Silas were put in prison back in Philippi (Acts 16:23-24). But here, Acts 17:9 says "…they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them." Jason walks out after paying the bond.

You got it, baker. Acts 17:10 says that on arriving in Berea, "…they went into the Jewish synagogue." That's the same move as in Thessalonica. And verse 11 says the Bereans received the message with great eagerness.

Good thought, but the text points somewhere else, baker. In Acts 17:10, Paul and Silas arrive in Berea and "…they went into the Jewish synagogue." The marketplace is where the Thessalonica troublemakers came from, not where this verse sends them.

I see why you'd think of her, baker. Lydia is the woman in Philippi whose house Paul and Silas went to (Acts 16:40). But Berea is a new city, and Acts 17:10 says they "…went into the Jewish synagogue."
That's the one, baker. Acts 17:11 says the Bereans "…received the message with great eagerness…" They also examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.

Nice thought, baker, but the text says nothing about money. Acts 17:11 says they "…received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day…" That's what makes them noble-minded.

That would be a big project, baker, but it isn't in the text. Paul and Silas simply "…went into the Jewish synagogue." that was already there (Acts 17:10). The Bereans are noble-minded because they "…received the message with great eagerness…" (Acts 17:11).

Yes, baker. Acts 17:12 says "…many of them believed…" That comes right after verse 11, where the Bereans "…examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true." They looked into it, and plenty of them came to believe.
That's the opposite, baker. Acts 17:12 says "…many of them believed…" The word is many, so the daily searching paid off.
Not this time, baker. Acts 17:12 says "…many of them believed…" None doesn't fit, because lots of them did. Examining the Scriptures every day led them to belief.
Right, baker. Acts 17:12 says many believed "…along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men." The verse names both the women and the men. It's a big, mixed crowd of people who believed.
Not quite, baker. Acts 17:12 says many believed "…along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men." So the statement is True. Both the women and the men are named there.

explanations.answer: Go there to stir up the crowds
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Acts 17:13 says they went to Berea themselves "…to incite and agitate the crowds." They don't stay home and fume. They travel after Paul.

explanations.answer: Send a warning letter to Caesar
explanations.explanation: Caesar's name did come up in Thessalonica (Acts 17:7), but no letter is mentioned. Acts 17:13 says they went to Berea themselves "…to incite and agitate the crowds." They go in person.

explanations.answer: Ask Jason to bring Paul back
explanations.explanation: I see the thinking, baker, but the text doesn't say that. Jason is the man who welcomed Paul and Silas into his home, and he isn't mentioned again. Acts 17:13 says the Jews from Thessalonica went to Berea "…to incite and agitate the crowds."
You got it, baker. Acts 17:14 says "The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast…" The word immediately tells you how fast they move.
Not quite, baker. The text says "The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast…" (Acts 17:14). No desert in this passage. The word is coast.
Good guess for a getaway, baker, but it's not in the text. Acts 17:14 says "The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast…" The word is coast, and they don't waste any time.
Not this time, baker. Acts 17:14 says "…Silas and Timothy remained in Berea." Timothy travels with Paul too (Acts 16:1-3). So the statement is False, because they stayed behind.
Yes, baker, False. Acts 17:14 says "…Silas and Timothy remained in Berea." Timothy travels with Paul too (Acts 16:1-3). He and Silas stay put while Paul goes on.
That's right, baker. Acts 17:15 says Paul's escorts "…brought him to Athens…" They get him there and then turn around.
A fair guess, since Paul does go to Corinth later (Acts 18:1), but it's not the city here. Acts 17:15 says the escorts "…brought him to Athens…" Athens is the answer.
Not this one, baker. Acts 17:15 says the escorts "…brought him to Athens…" Ephesus doesn't appear anywhere in this passage.

explanations.answer: Join Paul as soon as possible
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The escorts return with "…instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible." (Acts 17:15). Paul is in Athens, since that's where the escorts brought him. So the word to Silas and Timothy is to hurry.
Not quite, baker. The instructions in Acts 17:15 are for Silas and Timothy "…to join him as soon as possible." Nothing about heading back to Thessalonica. Their orders point toward Paul.

Waiting does sound sensible, but that's not the instruction. Acts 17:15 says the escorts brought "…instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible." They're to go to Paul, and they aren't told to wait.
